newsitem.title: GERMANY: Freightliner makes competitive leap with takeover.
newsitem.headline: Freightliner makes competitive leap with takeover.

text.p: U.S. truck maker Freightliner Corp, a unit of Germany's Daimler-Benz AG, has made a major competitive leap with its acquisition of Ford Motor Co's heavy truck business, Daimler's commercial vehicle chief said on Wednesday.
In an interview with Reuters, Kurt Lauk said the takeover would help Daimler commercial vehicle operations to reduce costs and vastly expand its sales network.
"It is the perfect acquisition," Lauk said from China in a telephone interview. "Freightliner has made a big step into a business in which we were under represented."
On Tuesday, Daimler announced it had won U.S. regulatory approval to buy Ford's heavy truck business, completing a deal first signed in May.
Although both Ford and Daimler have refused to disclose terms of the deal, Daimler said it would mean an additional $1 billion in sales revenues and unit sales of 20,000.
Lauk said Ford's business, which is strong in the construction market was a perfect fit with Freightliner's leading position in the long-haul truck market, but lacked in other business areas.
The marriage would also help to balance out sales for Daimler's U.S. truck operations as the two market segments react differently to economic cycles, he said.
"This will help stabilise Freightliner," Lauk said.
Freightliner further stood to benefit from the 250 Ford truck dealerships that Daimler will receive in the takeover, bringing its total number of U.S. truck dealerships to 550.
Freightliner could not have afforded to develop that many dealerships from scratch, he added.
The truck chief went on to say the deal would help Freightliner cut costs by increasing the size of parts orders it makes, enabling it to achieve greater economies of scale.
The manufacturing sites of Ford heavy trucks stand to move as part of Daimler's plans, probably to non-unionised areas, Lauk said adding he hoped to make a decision within a couple of months.
Daimler, which is already the world's leading truck maker, now has no further plans for takeovers in North America, Lauk said, adding it would take the company two years to digest the Ford takeover.
